bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
GFS2: remove transaction glock

GFS2 has a transaction glock, which must be grabbed for every
transaction, whose purpose
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 24972557b12ce8fd5b6c6847d0e2ee1837ddc13b
Author: Benjamin Marzinski <bmarzins@redhat.com>
Date:   Thu May 1 22:26:55 2014 -0500

    GFS2: remove transaction glock
    
    GFS2 has a transaction glock, which must be grabbed for every
    transaction, whose purpose is to deal with freezing the filesystem.
    Aside from this involving a large amount of locking, it is very easy to
    make the current fsfreeze code hang on unfreezing.
    
    This patch rewrites how gfs2 handles freezing
bic_trace_step.reason: The newly introduced function gfs2_log_release() at line +312 accesses sdp->sd_jdesc->jd_blocks (line +315-316) without any NULL check on sdp->sd_jdesc. This matches the root cause: a NULL pointer dereference when the journal descriptor has been deallocated. The code does not include any protection such as verifying sdp->sd_jdesc is non-NULL before dereferencing. Therefore, the vulnerable construct is present and not fixed in this commit.
